title: Spring Loop Derivation Canvas Demo
description: A recording-ready sequence of handwritten derivations where each result feeds the next step of a spring-loaded loop-the-loop design.

blocks.title: One connected derivation
blocks.content_html:
The goal is to design a spring launch that barely carries a cart through a vertical loop. Each canvas reads your handwritten lines, marks valid equations, and adds points when you reach the target.

The first derivation finds the required speed at the top of the loop. The next turns energy into a release height. Then you combine those two results and finish by sizing the spring compression.

blocks.title: Top-of-loop speed
blocks.prompt: At the top of the loop, the minimum-speed case has gravity supplying the centripetal force. Isolate v^2.
blocks.context_note: Carry forward: this result becomes the speed condition used in the height derivation.
hints: Rewrite with v^2 on the left.

blocks.title: Height as stored energy
blocks.prompt: Use conservation of energy from release height h to the top of the loop, then solve for h in terms of v^2.
blocks.context_note: Carry forward: the previous canvas gave v^2 = gR. Do not substitute it yet; first make a clean height formula.
hints: Divide the whole equation by g.
Leave v^2 in the formula so the top-speed result can drop in next.

blocks.title: Now connect the two results
blocks.content_html: The first canvas produced v2 = gR. The second produced h = v2/(2g) + 2R. The next canvas is the payoff: substitute the required top speed and simplify the minimum release height.

blocks.title: Minimum release height
blocks.prompt: Substitute the top-of-loop speed condition into the height formula and simplify h.
blocks.context_note: Carry forward: this height threshold is the amount of gravitational energy the launch spring must provide.

blocks.title: Spring compression
blocks.prompt: Finish the design. Set the spring energy equal to the gravitational energy needed for the release height h = 5R/2, then solve for the compression A.
blocks.context_note: Final link: the loop threshold from the previous canvas becomes the design requirement for the spring.
hints: First simplify the right side to 5mgR/2.
Take the positive square root because compression is a length.
